title: Closed-Loop AI Inverse Design Discovers 26.2%-Efficient Perovskite Solar-Cell Molecules
whyItMatters: Published in Science: couples high-throughput organic semiconductor synthesis with Bayesian optimization to inverse-design tailored hole-transport molecules achieving 26.2% (certified 25.9%) perovskite solar efficiency.
summary: An international team across Helmholtz-Institute Erlangen-Nürnberg (HI-ERN), FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), and UNIST demonstrated in Science a closed-loop inverse-design workflow uniting automated high-throughput synthesis with Bayesian optimization and interpretable molecular descriptors. Overcoming the sparse-data bottleneck in complex optoelectronic devices, the AI workflow proposed a minimal set of newly synthesized organic hole-transporting materials that reached up to 26.2% (independently certified 25.9%) power conversion efficiency in working perovskite solar cells.
technicalHighlights: First closed-loop inverse-design workflow delivering record-tier device-level organic semiconductors tailored for complex perovskite solar cells.
Links interpretable molecular descriptors to solar-cell efficiency via Bayesian optimization trained on high-throughput synthetic libraries.
Discovered novel hole-transporting molecules achieving up to 26.2% (independently certified 25.9%) power conversion efficiency.
caveats: Efficiency records were demonstrated on laboratory-scale perovskite solar cells; multi-decade outdoor stability and module-scale manufacturing remain ongoing commercialization challenges.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates end-to-end closed-loop inverse molecular design optimizing full optoelectronic device efficiency rather than isolated quantum proxies.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly accelerates next-generation clean-energy photovoltaics, OLEDs, and organic electronics.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science (Dec 2024) with physical synthesis and independently certified 25.9% solar-cell efficiency.
scoreRationale.velocity: Identified 26.2%-efficient hole-transport molecules from minimal closed-loop experimental suggestions.
